correctness.rationale: For a maximal independent set D in C(G), S=D∩V(G) must be a clique in G, hence |S|≤2 for triangle-free G. Every subdivision w_uv is forced in D iff both endpoints are outside S. An unchosen original v is undominated exactly when N_G(v)=S. Connectedness makes S=∅ allowed; |S|=1 exactly when chosen v has no degree-one neighbor; |S|=2 every original edge is allowed by triangle-freeness. This proves bijective exhaustive decomposition, the polynomial x^m+y∑_{ell(v)=0}x^{m+1-d(v)}+y²∑_{uv∈E}x^{m+3-d(u)-d(v)}, and total 1+m+#eligible vertices. Degree-sum coefficients and minimum multiplicities follow by exponent comparison; the known minimum m+3-D* is correctly credited. Independent direct central graph adjacency and subset enumeration matched full bivariate coefficients on 5 connected triangle-free examples of 3–6 original vertices. The all-graph proof is structural, not inferred from these samples.

value.rationale: Independent domination in central graphs is a natural graph invariant already singled out by a very recent optimization theorem. This result strengthens one minimum into a complete linear-sized parametrization of all maximal independent sets and a closed two-variable polynomial recovering edge degree-sums, useful for graph comparison and further enumerative work. The finite class is all connected triangle-free input graphs rather than an arbitrary size slice.
